Principle 20: Famous Places in Korea
Korea’s Geographical Location
The land of Korea is a peninsula located between China and Japan and is surrounded by three seas: the East Sea, the West Sea, and the South Sea.
Its geographical landscape is beautiful and filled with many wonderful places to visit.
Hot Spots to Visit in Korea
Our country has many attractive places to visit that are natural, historical, and sometimes man-made.
Such places include the Bulguk Temple, Soungni-San National Park, and Independence-Hall.
The Korean Folk Village in Suwon
One very interesting place to visit is the Korean Folk Village located near the city of Suwon in Gyoung-gi Province, not far from the capital of Seoul.
When you visit there, you can witness a traditional wedding ceremony, taste a variety of traditional foods, and you can observe how Koreans lived during ancient times.
It is a very popular attraction for many foreign visitors.
The Ancient Capital of Gyeong-ju
Another attractive destination is Gyeong-ju.
Gyeong-ju is the old capital of the Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom was its most powerful during the 8th century.
Many people regard Gyeong-ju as a museum without walls.
Koreans refer to it as this because it contains many of the old remains of the Shilla Dynasty.
Korea’s Natural Paradise—Jeju Island
Perhaps the most famous natural wonder of Korea is an island called Jeju.
Jeju island is my favorite place to go for vacation.
There are so many fun things to do there and many beautiful spots to visit.
I like going to Mt. Halla.
It is in the center of Jeju island and is a really high mountain.
Mt. Halla is the highest mountain in South Korea; it’s almost 2,000 meters high (about 6,500 feet).
